flooring_installation.unit_description: per square foot of floor area

medium_room.description: 300 sq ft - master bedroom or living room

large_area.description: 1,000 sq ft - whole floor or open concept space

full_house.description: 2,000 sq ft - average single family home

carpet_mid_grade.notes: Nylon carpet with good padding, stain resistant

carpet_premium.notes: High-end wool or premium nylon, thick padding

vinyl_plank_basic.notes: Basic vinyl plank flooring (LVP), thin wear layer

vinyl_plank_mid.notes: Mid-grade LVP with 12-20 mil wear layer, waterproof

vinyl_plank_premium.notes: Premium LVP, 20+ mil wear layer, realistic wood grain

laminate_premium.notes: High-quality laminate, AC4-AC5 rating, moisture resistant

hardwood_oak_prefinished.notes: 3/4 inch solid red oak, prefinished, standard grade

hardwood_oak_unfinished.notes: 3/4 inch solid oak, unfinished, requires site finishing

hardwood_exotic.notes: Brazilian cherry, teak, or other exotic species

engineered_hardwood_basic.notes: Thin veneer engineered wood, 3mm wear layer

engineered_hardwood_premium.notes: Thick veneer engineered wood, 5-6mm wear layer, can be refinished

tile_porcelain.notes: Porcelain tile, more durable than ceramic

tile_mortar_and_grout.notes: Thinset mortar, grout, sealer for tile installation

flooring_installer_rate.occupation: Floor Layers (except Carpet, Wood, Hard Tiles)
flooring_installer_rate.notes: BLS 2024 data, loaded rate includes overhead and insurance

carpet_installation.notes: Includes stretching, seaming, trimming. Does not include removal.

hardwood_installation_nail_down.notes: Nail down installation for 3/4 inch solid hardwood

hardwood_installation_glue_down.notes: Glue down for engineered hardwood or parquet

hardwood_sanding_and_finishing.typical_time: 2-4 days for 300 sq ft (including drying time)
hardwood_sanding_and_finishing.notes: For unfinished hardwood: sanding, staining (optional), 3 coats polyurethane

tile_installation.notes: Includes layout, cutting, mortar, grouting, sealing. Complex patterns cost more.

old_flooring_removal.notes: Removal and disposal. Tile removal is on the high end, carpet on low end.

floor_leveling.notes: Self-leveling compound for uneven concrete slabs

master_bedroom_carpet.notes: 350 sq ft mid-grade carpet installed over existing subfloor

living_room_hardwood.notes: 400 sq ft prefinished oak hardwood, nail down installation

kitchen_tile.notes: 200 sq ft porcelain tile with standard pattern

whole_house_vinyl_plank.notes: 1500 sq ft mid-grade LVP, includes removal of old carpet

bathroom_tile_floor.notes: Small bathroom (60 sq ft) ceramic tile

red_flags: Charging >$5/sq ft for basic carpet installation labor (should be $1-2.50/sq ft)
Requiring 'premium underlayment' for basic laminate when standard foam works fine
Pushing exotic hardwood when domestic oak would work equally well
Charging tile installation rates ($8-12/sq ft labor) for simple vinyl plank ($1.75-3.50/sq ft)
Claiming subfloor damage without showing you the actual damage
Requiring full subfloor replacement when only spot repairs needed
Charging >$4/sq ft for old flooring removal (should be $0.75-3/sq ft depending on type)
Bundling 'required' supplies at marked-up prices (transition strips, quarter round)
Pushing glue-down installation for engineered hardwood when floating is acceptable and cheaper
Insisting all existing baseboards must be replaced (usually can reuse)
Adding 20%+ 'waste factor' - standard is 5-10% for most flooring types
Charging separately for 'measuring' or 'consultation' that should be included in quote
common_upsells: Premium moisture barrier when standard vapor barrier sufficient
Exotic wood species when domestic hardwood would look similar
Glue-down installation when floating floor would work
Complete baseboard replacement when removal and reinstall possible
Decorative tile patterns or borders that significantly increase labor cost

cost_factors.room_shape: Irregular shapes, angles, closets increase labor 15-30%
cost_factors.furniture_moving: Typically $50-150 per room if contractor moves furniture
cost_factors.stairs: Stair installation costs 2-3x more per sq ft than flat surfaces
cost_factors.pattern_matching: Tile patterns, hardwood borders, carpet seams increase labor 20-40%

regional_notes.high_cost_areas: Expect labor rates 25-40% higher in NYC, SF, Boston
regional_notes.low_cost_areas: Southern and rural areas typically 10-20% below national average
regional_notes.seasonal: Flooring contractors may discount 10-15% in winter slow season
